claims.subject: jv_brahma_ram
claims.summary: Brahmā describes Jāmbavān emerging when he yawned.
claims.speaker: Brahmā
claims.note: Narrated origin, not an ordinary biological father claim.

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: Jāmbavān recalls circling Trivikrama at Bali’s sacrifice.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: Verse 15 gives no count of circuits. No yuga-to-calendar conversion.

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He argues that Aṅgada should be protected as leader.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He turns to Hanumān to enable the mission.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He recalls seeing Garuḍa and compares Hanumān’s abilities.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He recounts Hanumān’s origins and urges action.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: No forgetting-curse claim is extracted from the site’s commentary.

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: Wounded Jāmbavān identifies Vibhīṣaṇa by voice.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He treats Hanumān’s survival as crucial to recovery.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: An inquiry about Hanumān, not an address to him.

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He directs Hanumān to fetch four restorative herbs.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: The battlefield account calls him Prajāpati’s son.
claims.speaker: narrator
claims.note: Linked translation identifies Prajāpati here as Brahmā; retain that qualification.

claims.subject: jv_sb8
claims.summary: Jāmbavān proclaims Vāmana’s victory with an instrument.
claims.speaker: narrator
claims.note: No circumambulation count is given in this verse.

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: The two fight for twenty-eight days.
claims.speaker: Śuka

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: Jāmbavān identifies his opponent as Viṣṇu.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: A character’s theological recognition, not a database same-person merge.

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: He associates his addressee with the bridge and Laṅkā campaign.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: Rāma is not explicitly named in the verse; the episode identification is contextual. Does not itself say the speaker personally witnessed every listed deed.

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: Jāmbavatī is identified as Jāmbavān’s daughter.
claims.speaker: Śuka

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: He presents the jewel and his daughter to Kṛṣṇa.
claims.speaker: Śuka

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: The jewel becomes a plaything for his young son.
claims.speaker: Śuka
claims.note: The verse leaves the son unnamed. Do not automatically label him Sukumāra.

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: Jāmbavān kills the lion that killed Prasena.
claims.speaker: Śuka
claims.note: This is not a claim that Jāmbavān killed Prasena.

claims.subject: jv_son_sb10
claims.summary: The child plays with the Syamantaka jewel.
claims.speaker: Śuka

claims.subject: jv_jambavati_sb10
claims.summary: Sāmba is listed among Jāmbavatī’s sons.
claims.speaker: Śuka

claims.subject: jv_samba_sb
claims.summary: The later episode again names Sāmba’s mother.
claims.speaker: Śuka

claims.subject: jv_yadu_boys_sb11
claims.summary: The Yadu boys disguise Sāmba to test the sages.
claims.speaker: Śuka

claims.subject: jv_sages_sb11
claims.summary: The sages foretell a club destructive to their dynasty.
claims.speaker: sages
claims.note: A reported prediction addressed to the boys; not a causal edge from Jāmbavān.

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He reports twenty-one circuits of the earth during Trivikrama’s time.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: The object is the earth, not explicitly Trivikrama’s body. This numerical passage was omitted from the initial dossier.

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He recalls collecting herbs under divine orders for nectar-churning.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: The speaker uses a plural rendered as royal we by the linked translator. No claim that these are the later four healing herbs.

claims.subject: jv_amrita_herbs
claims.summary: The collected herbs belong to the recalled nectar-churning operation.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān

claims.subject: jv_ram
claims.summary: He urges Aṅgada to consider Rāma’s intention before acting.
claims.speaker: Jāmbavān
claims.note: This short passage does not explicitly state a ban on unauthorized rescue, despite expanded retellings.

claims.subject: ram6_angada
claims.summary: Aṅgada proposes returning with Sītā rather than only reporting.
claims.speaker: Aṅgada
claims.note: A proposed action, not a completed rescue.

claims.subject: jv_kin_vp
claims.summary: Kṛṣṇa’s kinsfolk perform rites after receiving news of his supposed death.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: The report is mistaken within the narrative; Kṛṣṇa is still fighting.

claims.subject: jv_funeral_rites_vp
claims.summary: The offerings are narrated as sustaining Kṛṣṇa during the duel.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: A claim within this telling, not an empirical statement about ritual efficacy.

claims.subject: vp4_13_jambavant
claims.summary: Jāmbavant lacks food and weakens as the fight continues.
claims.speaker: Parāśara

claims.subject: jv_nurse_vp
claims.summary: The nurse’s song recounts the jewel’s passage through the lion and bear.
claims.speaker: Parāśara

claims.subject: vp4_15_kṛṣṇa
claims.summary: Kṛṣṇa hears the nurse before approaching the jewel.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: Hearing is not necessarily a reciprocal conversation.

claims.subject: jv_kin_vp
claims.summary: The Yādavas suspect Kṛṣṇa after Prasena disappears.
claims.speaker: Parāśara
claims.note: This encodes suspicion, not Kṛṣṇa killing Prasena. The subject is the collectively described Yādavas.

claims.subject: vp4_13_satrajita
claims.summary: Satrājit voices the accusation that spreads through the populace.
claims.speaker: Satrājit
claims.note: An attributed accusation, contradicted by the narrated lion episode; not an actual killing edge.

claims.subject: jv_dvaraka_residents_sb
claims.summary: The residents seek Kṛṣṇa’s return through Candrabhāgā / Durgā.
claims.speaker: Śuka
claims.note: Compare the VP funerary-offering narrative; do not infer either practice is absent from every other witness.

claims.subject: jv_sb10
claims.summary: The narrator says Jāmbavān fights Kṛṣṇa without recognizing his divine status, taking him for an ordinary person.
claims.speaker: Śuka
claims.note: Initial narrated belief, superseded by the recognition in 10.56.26. Not an objective identity assertion or a claim of deliberate opposition after recognition.

observations.subject: jv_ram
observations.note: Narrative capacity claim; no conversion to modern distance.

observations.subject: ram6_angada
observations.note: Jāmbavān subsequently invokes protection of the leader.
Site numbering; not asserted to equal a critical-edition locator. This is a third textual witness, not independent historical corroboration.

observations.subject: jv_ram
observations.note: Circuits of the earth; kept distinct from the unnumbered Trivikrama circumambulation in 4.65.15.

open_work: Collate Sanskrit and critical-edition numbering before philological claims.
Review more Jāmbavān passages and alternative Syamantaka tellings.
Retain disagreements in duration and names instead of harmonizing them.
